--- title: "Support Vector Machines" author: "Diego Villalba" date: today lang: en format: html: toc: true toc-depth: 3 toc-title: "Contents" number-sections: true code-fold: true code-tools: true code-summary: "Show code" fig-align: center theme: cosmo highlight-style: github smooth-scroll: true pdf: toc: true toc-depth: 3 number-sections: true documentclass: scrbook papersize: letter fontsize: 11pt geometry: margin=2.5cm keep-tex: false execute: echo: true warning: false message: false cache: false bibliography: referencias_svm.bib crossref: fig-title: "Figure" tbl-title: "Table" eq-prefix: "Eq." jupyter: python3 --- Support Vector Machines (SVM) represent one of the most theoretically elegant frameworks in supervised learning. Developed by Vladimir Vapnik and colleagues in the 1990s [@vapnik1995nature; @cortes1995support], SVMs combine three core concepts: maximum-margin hyperplanes, Lagrangian duality, and the *kernel trick* to operate in high-dimensional feature spaces without explicit coordinate transformations. Unlike logistic regression (which seeks any separating boundary), SVMs find the *optimal* boundary maximizing the minimal geometric distance to training instances. This property links margin maximization to Statistical Learning Theory and generalization capacity [@hastie2009elements]. This chapter develops SVM theory from geometric foundations to practical extensions, covering soft-margin formulations, kernel tricks, Support Vector Regression (SVR), and probability calibration. ## Motivation: Maximum-Margin Classification ### Multiple Separating Hyperplanes For a linearly separable dataset, infinitely many hyperplanes separate training instances perfectly. Which boundary should be selected? ### Why Margins Matter SVMs select the unique decision boundary that maximizes the **margin**: the geometric distance from the boundary to the nearest training instance. Maximizing margin minimizes Vapnik-Chervonenkis (VC) capacity, bounding generalization error independently of input dimension $d$ [@vapnik1995nature]. $$ \text{margin} = \frac{2}{\|\mathbf{w}\|} $$ Maximizing margin corresponds directly to minimizing $\|\mathbf{w}\|$. ::: {#cell-fig-svm-multiple-hyperplanes .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import numpy as np import plotly.graph_objects as go np.random.seed(42) X_neg = np.column_stack([ np.random.uniform(0.5, 2.5, 12), np.random.uniform(3.5, 6.0, 12) ]) X_pos = np.column_stack([ np.random.uniform(3.5, 6.0, 12), np.random.uniform(0.5, 3.0, 12) ]) fig = go.Figure() fig.add_trace(go.Scatter( x=X_neg[:, 0], y=X_neg[:, 1], mode='markers', name='Class −1', marker=dict(color='#4C72B0', size=10, symbol='circle') )) fig.add_trace(go.Scatter( x=X_pos[:, 0], y=X_pos[:, 1], mode='markers', name='Class +1', marker=dict(color='#DD8452', size=10, symbol='square') )) x_line = np.linspace(0, 7, 200) y_opt = 6.5 - x_line fig.add_trace(go.Scatter( x=x_line, y=y_opt, mode='lines', name='Maximum Margin (Optimal)', line=dict(color='#2c4f8c', width=3) )) configs = [ (5.5 - x_line, 'rgba(100,100,100,0.5)', 'Alternative Boundary 1'), (7.0 - 1.3 * x_line, 'rgba(130,130,130,0.5)', 'Alternative Boundary 2'), (5.0 - 0.7 * x_line, 'rgba(160,160,160,0.5)', 'Alternative Boundary 3'), ] for y_alt, col, name in configs: fig.add_trace(go.Scatter( x=x_line, y=y_alt, mode='lines', name=name, line=dict(color=col, width=1.5, dash='dot') )) fig.update_layout( title='Multiple Separating Hyperplanes: Unique Maximum Margin Selection', xaxis_title='Feature 1', yaxis_title='Feature 2', xaxis=dict(range=[0, 7]), yaxis=dict(range=[0, 7]), height=480, template='plotly_white', legend=dict(orientation='h', yanchor='top', y=-0.18, xanchor='center', x=0.5) ) fig.show() ``` ::: {#fig-svm-multiple-hyperplanes .cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` Multiple valid separating hyperplanes for linearly separable data. The maximum-margin boundary (solid blue line) is unique and optimal. ::: ::: ## Hard-Margin SVM (Linearly Separable Data) ### Primal Formulation $$ \min_{\mathbf{w},\, b} \quad \frac{1}{2}\|\mathbf{w}\|^2 $$ $$ \text{subject to} \quad y_i(\mathbf{w}^\top \mathbf{x}_i + b) \geq 1, \quad \forall\, i = 1, \dots, n $$ {#eq-svm-primal} ### Support Vectors and Dual Formulation Points satisfying $y_i(\mathbf{w}^\top \mathbf{x}_i + b) = 1$ are **support vectors**. The dual optimization problem is: $$ \max_{\boldsymbol{\alpha}} \quad \sum_{i=1}^n \alpha_i - \frac{1}{2}\sum_{i=1}^n\sum_{j=1}^n \alpha_i \alpha_j y_i y_j \mathbf{x}_i^\top \mathbf{x}_j $$ {#eq-svm-dual} $$ \text{subject to} \quad \alpha_i \geq 0, \quad \sum_{i=1}^n \alpha_i y_i = 0 $$ The dual decision function evaluates to: $$ f(\mathbf{x}) = \text{sgn}\!\left(\sum_{i \in \mathcal{S}} \alpha_i y_i \mathbf{x}_i^\top \mathbf{x} + b\right) $$ {#eq-svm-decision} ::: {#cell-fig-svm-hard-margin .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} import numpy as np import plotly.graph_objects as go np.random.seed(7) X_pos = np.column_stack([ np.random.uniform(3.2, 5.5, 10), np.random.uniform(3.2, 5.5, 10) ]) X_neg = np.column_stack([ np.random.uniform(0.5, 2.8, 10), np.random.uniform(0.5, 2.8, 10) ]) w = np.array([1.0, 1.0]) / np.sqrt(2) b_unnorm = -6.0 / np.sqrt(2) dist_pos = (X_pos @ w + b_unnorm) dist_neg = (X_neg @ w + b_unnorm) sv_pos_idx = np.argmin(dist_pos) sv_neg_idx = np.argmax(dist_neg) margin_pos = dist_pos[sv_pos_idx] margin_neg = -dist_neg[sv_neg_idx] x_line = np.linspace(0, 7, 300) y_hyp = 6.0 - x_line y_marg_pos = 6.0 + margin_pos*np.sqrt(2) - x_line y_marg_neg = 6.0 - margin_neg*np.sqrt(2) - x_line fig = go.Figure() fig.add_trace(go.Scatter( x=np.concatenate([x_line, x_line[::-1]]), y=np.concatenate([y_marg_pos, y_marg_neg[::-1]]), fill='toself', fillcolor='rgba(150,150,150,0.12)', line=dict(color='rgba(0,0,0,0)'), name='Margin Band' )) fig.add_trace(go.Scatter( x=x_line, y=y_marg_pos, mode='lines', name='Margin +1', line=dict(color='#DD8452', width=1.5, dash='dash') )) fig.add_trace(go.Scatter( x=x_line, y=y_marg_neg, mode='lines', name='Margin −1', line=dict(color='#4C72B0', width=1.5, dash='dash') )) fig.add_trace(go.Scatter( x=x_line, y=y_hyp, mode='lines', name='Optimal Hyperplane', line=dict(color='#2c4f8c', width=2.5) )) mask_neg = np.ones(len(X_neg), dtype=bool) mask_neg[sv_neg_idx] = False fig.add_trace(go.Scatter( x=X_neg[mask_neg, 0], y=X_neg[mask_neg, 1], mode='markers', name='Class −1', marker=dict(color='#4C72B0', size=10) )) mask_pos = np.ones(len(X_pos), dtype=bool) mask_pos[sv_pos_idx] = False fig.add_trace(go.Scatter( x=X_pos[mask_pos, 0], y=X_pos[mask_pos, 1], mode='markers', name='Class +1', marker=dict(color='#DD8452', size=10, symbol='square') )) fig.add_trace(go.Scatter( x=[X_neg[sv_neg_idx, 0]], y=[X_neg[sv_neg_idx, 1]], mode='markers', name='Support Vector −1', marker=dict(color='#4C72B0', size=14, line=dict(color='black', width=2.5)) )) fig.add_trace(go.Scatter( x=[X_pos[sv_pos_idx, 0]], y=[X_pos[sv_pos_idx, 1]], mode='markers', name='Support Vector +1', marker=dict(color='#DD8452', size=14, symbol='square', line=dict(color='black', width=2.5)) )) fig.update_layout( title='Hard-Margin SVM: Optimal Hyperplane & Support Vectors', xaxis_title='Feature 1', yaxis_title='Feature 2', xaxis=dict(range=[0, 7]), yaxis=dict(range=[0, 7]), height=500, template='plotly_white', legend=dict(orientation='h', yanchor='top', y=-0.18, xanchor='center', x=0.5) ) fig.show() ``` ::: {#fig-svm-hard-margin .cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` Hard-margin SVM on linearly separable 2D data. Support vectors highlighted with black borders. ::: ::: ## Soft-Margin SVM (Non-Separable Data) $$ \min_{\mathbf{w},\, b,\, \boldsymbol{\xi}} \quad \frac{1}{2}\|\mathbf{w}\|^2 + C\sum_{i=1}^n \xi_i $$ {#eq-svm-soft-primal} $$ \text{subject to} \quad y_i(\mathbf{w}^\top \mathbf{x}_i + b) \geq 1 - \xi_i, \quad \xi_i \geq 0 $$ Regularization hyperparameter $C > 0$ controls the trade-off between maximizing margin width and penalizing margin slack violations [@cortes1995support]. ::: {#cell-fig-svm-soft-C .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} import numpy as np import plotly.graph_objects as go np.random.seed(21) n = 30 X_pos = np.column_stack([ np.random.normal(3.5, 0.9, n), np.random.normal(3.5, 0.9, n) ]) X_neg = np.column_stack([ np.random.normal(2.0, 0.9, n), np.random.normal(2.0, 0.9, n) ]) X = np.vstack([X_pos, X_neg]) y = np.array([1]*n + [-1]*n) def svm_soft_approx(X, y, C): mu_pos = X[y == 1].mean(axis=0) mu_neg = X[y == -1].mean(axis=0) w_dir = mu_pos - mu_neg w_dir = w_dir / np.linalg.norm(w_dir) mid = (mu_pos + mu_neg) / 2.0 margin_scale = 1.0 / (1.0 + 0.3 * np.log1p(C)) b = -np.dot(w_dir, mid) return w_dir, b, margin_scale C_values = [0.01, 0.1, 1.0, 10.0, 100.0] x_line = np.linspace(-1, 7, 300) frames = [] for C in C_values: w, b, ms = svm_soft_approx(X, y, C) y_hyp = -(w[0]*x_line + b) / w[1] y_mp = -(w[0]*x_line + b - ms) / w[1] y_mn = -(w[0]*x_line + b + ms) / w[1] scores = X @ w + b correct = (scores * y) >= 0 violated = ~correct frame_data = [ go.Scatter( x=np.concatenate([x_line, x_line[::-1]]), y=np.concatenate([y_mp, y_mn[::-1]]), fill='toself', fillcolor='rgba(150,150,150,0.15)', line=dict(color='rgba(0,0,0,0)'), name='Margin Band' ), go.Scatter(x=x_line, y=y_mp, mode='lines', line=dict(color='#DD8452', dash='dash', width=1.5), name='Margin +1'), go.Scatter(x=x_line, y=y_mn, mode='lines', line=dict(color='#4C72B0', dash='dash', width=1.5), name='Margin −1'), go.Scatter(x=x_line, y=y_hyp, mode='lines', line=dict(color='#2c4f8c', width=2.5), name='Hyperplane'), go.Scatter(x=X[y==1][correct[y==1], 0], y=X[y==1][correct[y==1], 1], mode='markers', name='Class +1', marker=dict(color='#DD8452', size=9, symbol='square')), go.Scatter(x=X[y==-1][correct[y==-1], 0], y=X[y==-1][correct[y==-1], 1], mode='markers', name='Class −1', marker=dict(color='#4C72B0', size=9)), go.Scatter(x=X[violated, 0], y=X[violated, 1], mode='markers', name='Misclassified', marker=dict(color='red', size=10, symbol='x', line=dict(width=2))), ] frames.append(go.Frame(data=frame_data, name=str(C))) w0, b0, ms0 = svm_soft_approx(X, y, 1.0) y_hyp0 = -(w0[0]*x_line + b0) / w0[1] y_mp0 = -(w0[0]*x_line + b0 - ms0) / w0[1] y_mn0 = -(w0[0]*x_line + b0 + ms0) / w0[1] scores0 = X @ w0 + b0 correct0 = (scores0 * y) >= 0 violated0 = ~correct0 fig = go.Figure( data=[ go.Scatter( x=np.concatenate([x_line, x_line[::-1]]), y=np.concatenate([y_mp0, y_mn0[::-1]]), fill='toself', fillcolor='rgba(150,150,150,0.15)', line=dict(color='rgba(0,0,0,0)'), name='Margin Band' ), go.Scatter(x=x_line, y=y_mp0, mode='lines', line=dict(color='#DD8452', dash='dash', width=1.5), name='Margin +1'), go.Scatter(x=x_line, y=y_mn0, mode='lines', line=dict(color='#4C72B0', dash='dash', width=1.5), name='Margin −1'), go.Scatter(x=x_line, y=y_hyp0, mode='lines', line=dict(color='#2c4f8c', width=2.5), name='Hyperplane'), go.Scatter(x=X[y==1][correct0[y==1], 0], y=X[y==1][correct0[y==1], 1], mode='markers', name='Class +1', marker=dict(color='#DD8452', size=9, symbol='square')), go.Scatter(x=X[y==-1][correct0[y==-1], 0], y=X[y==-1][correct0[y==-1], 1], mode='markers', name='Class −1', marker=dict(color='#4C72B0', size=9)), go.Scatter(x=X[violated0, 0], y=X[violated0, 1], mode='markers', name='Misclassified', marker=dict(color='red', size=10, symbol='x', line=dict(width=2))), ], frames=frames ) slider_steps = [] for C in C_values: slider_steps.append(dict( args=[[str(C)], dict(frame=dict(duration=300), mode='immediate', transition=dict(duration=200))], label=str(C), method='animate' )) fig.update_layout( title='Soft-Margin Parameter C Trade-off', xaxis_title='Feature 1', yaxis_title='Feature 2', template='plotly_white', height=490, sliders=[dict(currentvalue=dict(prefix='C = ', font=dict(size=14)), steps=slider_steps, pad=dict(t=50))] ) fig.show() ``` ::: {#fig-svm-soft-c .cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` Impact of regularization parameter C on soft-margin decision boundaries. ::: ::: ## The Kernel Trick $$ K(\mathbf{x}_i, \mathbf{x}_j) = \phi(\mathbf{x}_i)^\top \phi(\mathbf{x}_j) $$ {#eq-kernel-def} Common Kernels: - **Linear:** $K(\mathbf{x}_i, \mathbf{x}_j) = \mathbf{x}_i^\top \mathbf{x}_j$ - **Polynomial:** $K(\mathbf{x}_i, \mathbf{x}_j) = (\gamma\, \mathbf{x}_i^\top \mathbf{x}_j + r)^d$ - **RBF (Gaussian):** $K(\mathbf{x}_i, \mathbf{x}_j) = \exp\!\left(-\gamma\,\|\mathbf{x}_i - \mathbf{x}_j\|^2\right)$ {#eq-rbf-kernel} ::: {#cell-fig-kernel-transform .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} import numpy as np import plotly.graph_objects as go from plotly.subplots import make_subplots np.random.seed(3) x_neg = np.random.uniform(-1.0, 1.0, 20) x_pos = np.concatenate([ np.random.uniform(-2.5, -1.2, 10), np.random.uniform(1.2, 2.5, 10) ]) phi_neg = np.column_stack([x_neg, x_neg**2]) phi_pos = np.column_stack([x_pos, x_pos**2]) fig = make_subplots( rows=1, cols=2, subplot_titles=[ 'Original Space ℝ¹ (Non-Separable)', 'Transformed Space ℝ² φ(x)=(x, x²) (Separable)' ] ) jitter_neg = np.random.uniform(-0.05, 0.05, len(x_neg)) jitter_pos = np.random.uniform(-0.05, 0.05, len(x_pos)) fig.add_trace(go.Scatter( x=x_neg, y=jitter_neg, mode='markers', name='Class −1', marker=dict(color='#4C72B0', size=10) ), row=1, col=1) fig.add_trace(go.Scatter( x=x_pos, y=jitter_pos, mode='markers', name='Class +1', marker=dict(color='#DD8452', size=10, symbol='square') ), row=1, col=1) fig.add_trace(go.Scatter( x=phi_neg[:, 0], y=phi_neg[:, 1], mode='markers', name='Class −1 (φ)', marker=dict(color='#4C72B0', size=10), showlegend=False ), row=1, col=2) fig.add_trace(go.Scatter( x=phi_pos[:, 0], y=phi_pos[:, 1], mode='markers', name='Class +1 (φ)', marker=dict(color='#DD8452', size=10, symbol='square'), showlegend=False ), row=1, col=2) x_sep = np.linspace(-3, 3, 100) fig.add_trace(go.Scatter( x=x_sep, y=np.full_like(x_sep, 1.3), mode='lines', name='Separating Hyperplane', line=dict(color='#2c4f8c', width=2.5, dash='dash') ), row=1, col=2) fig.update_layout( height=430, template='plotly_white', title='Kernel Trick: 1D Non-Separable to 2D Separable Mapping' ) fig.show() ``` ::: {#fig-kernel-transform .cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` Non-linear 1D input space transformed into linearly separable 2D feature space via φ(x) = (x, x²). ::: ::: ## Support Vector Regression (SVR) SVR introduces an $\varepsilon$-insensitive loss tube around the target regression function, ignoring error magnitudes below $\varepsilon$. ## Platt Probability Calibration {#sec-platt} Sigmoid calibration maps uncalibrated SVM output scores $f(\mathbf{x})$ into well-calibrated posterior probabilities [@platt1999probabilistic]: $$ P(y = 1 \mid f(\mathbf{x})) = \frac{1}{1 + \exp(Af(\mathbf{x}) + B)} $$ {#eq-platt} ## Summary SVMs optimize maximum-margin hyperplanes using convex quadratic programming. The kernel trick enables non-linear decision boundaries, while Support Vector Regression adapts loss tolerances for continuous target estimation [@chang2011libsvm]. ## References ::: {#refs} :::
